newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chinese troops inspect venue of Hong Kong handover.
newsitem.headline: Chinese troops inspect venue of Hong Kong handover.

text.p: A contingent of Chinese troops caused a stir on Wednesday when they arrived to inspect the yet-to-be-completed grand hall where Britain will hand Hong Kong to China in a solemn ceremony at midnight on June 30.
But a Hong Kong police spokesman said the group were members of the People's Liberation Army (PLA) orchestra, set to join the festivities -- and not highly trained security experts.
"It is the sole responsibility of the Hong Kong police to ensure the safety of the venue of the handover ceremony," a police spokesman said.

About 30 members of the PLA orchestra, wearing distinctive new casual clothing issued to the elite members of the future Hong Kong garrison, were conducted around the hall at the Convention and Exhibition Centre as workmen rushed to put the finishing touches to the building.
The troops declined to comment to waiting reporters but a police source said they had expressed satisfaction with what they saw.
Hong Kong has tightened security ahead of the arrival of more than 4,000 international dignitaries for the ceremony marking the end of 156 years of British rule.
President Jiang Zemin will represent China and royal heir Prince Charles will be Britain's chief representative.

Many Hong Kong people recall with horror the PLA's suppression of youthful pro-democracy demonstrators around Beijing's Tiananmen Square in June 1989, killing hundreds, and anxiously view the stationing of Chinese troops here.
An advance force of nearly 200 troops is already in place preparing the way for the future garrison.

Britain baulked at first but then gave in to Chinese requests to allow in an additional 509 armed troops, three hours before the transfer of sovereignty, so they could be in place when midnight strikes and Hong Kong becomes Chinese.
The PLA musicians will mingle with the Hong Kong police, boy scouts, girl guides and kung-fu clubs for a spectacular musical parade at next week's handover.
This will be the first time the PLA has performed in Hong Kong or joined crowds in the territory.
